utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honour, we are ready to proceed. My name is Mark Harmon and I will be representing the Prosecutor’s office this morning. PRESIDING JUDGE: May I have other appearances please? Madam Vidovic

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honour. My name is Vashija Vidovic Minister counsellor with the Embassy of Bosnia Herzegovina representing Bosnia Herzegovina at this hearing. PRESIDING JUDGE: Thank you. Additional appearances?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: I’m Jadranka Slokovi} GLUMAC I’m a lawyer from Zagreb and I’m the legal representative of Mr. Jelavic and I have also been authorised by Mr. Jelavic to clarify some issues related to the said documents as his representative. PRESIDING JUDGE: Are you familiar with the documents Ms. GLUMAC. Let me put it this way. Rather than familiar with the documents are you familiar with the central archive so that you can tell the Tribunal whether the documents exit, which documents exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: I do possess some information about that and I will relay that information on behalf of Mr. Jelavic or rather the Ministry of Defence. I do not have full proposal, full information but I do have some information about that. PRESIDING JUDGE: Thank you. We’ll see as we proceed along what information you have and whether Mr. Jelavic has complied with the order by you coming here. Thank you. Mr. Harmon

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, since the last hearing I can report to the court that we have not received a single document in response to the subpoena duces tecum. And I have a series of exhibits which I would like to present to the court. if I could be permitted to do so. PRESIDING JUDGE: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first exhibit, filed exhibit, your Honour, exhibit 1 is a letter which is directed to me from Judge Vidovic informing me of the steps that she took after your Honour issued a court order on 24th February 1997, that would be my exhibit no. 1. Exhibits 2, 3, 4 and 5 are exhibits which show proof of service, including exhibit no. 5, I sorry, exhibit no. 4 which shows that Mr. Jelavic was served with your order on 25th February 1997. PRESIDING JUDGE: You’ve shown those to Ms. GLUMAC.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had no information what so ever that there was going to be an appearance by a representative of Mr. Jelavic today, so I am certainly happy to recess at some point and make copies available to her. But I didn’t anticipate any appearance today by her. PRESIDING JUDGE: Are you going to make reference to these exhibits at this moment or can we just have them copied and Ms. GLUMAC receive a copy. Ms. GLUMAC do you a copy of the letter from Judge Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, I do

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a series of other exhibits, but if your Honour would like to take a moment to study those before I announce the other exhibits. PRESIDING JUDGE: Many of them are in Serbo Croat and I’m trying but I am not at that point yet. Let’s have a copy made of these and then we provide them to Ms. GLUMAC.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Should I proceed with identifying the next exhibit your Honour PRESIDING JUDGE: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The next exhibit, your Honour, exhibit 6 would be a letter directed to your Honour from the Prime Minister informing you of steps that he has taken . Your Honour, I have had this document since late yesterday and I have had this document submitted to the translation section and I have an official translation of this document. So this would be item no. 6. PRESIDING JUDGE: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Item no. 7, your Honour, is a letter date 18 February 1997 and it is to Mr. Jelavic from the Prime Minister requesting that Mr. Jelavic comply with the subpoena duces tecum. Again, you Honour, I have had this document submitted to translation and I have an official translation of the document attached. Item no. 8, your Honour, is a reply from Mr. Jelavic dated 19 February 1997 to the Prime Minister. I have a copy of an official translation of that document attached to the original as well. That would be the Prosecutor’s exhibit no. 8. PRESIDING JUDGE: And that is a, Mr Harmon would you repeat that for me, please. MR. HARMON; Yes, your Honour, item no. 8 is a reply to the prime Minister by Mr. Jelavic. It’s a reply to the document no, exhibit no. 7 and the date on the reply is 19 February 1997. Prosecutor’s exhibit no. 9, your Honour, is a letter dated 21 February, 1997 to Mr. Jelavic from the Prime Minister requesting that he appear at the hearing today to provide answers concerning the failure to comply with the subpoena duces tecum or to designate a representative who is familiar with the location and the contents of the archives and who will be able to explain what steps have been taken to comply with this subpoena duces tecum. I have also submitted this document to translation and there’s an official translation of this document attached. PRESIDING JUDGE: Does that complete the exhibits that you wish to offer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have two more exhibits, your Honour. Exhibit no. 10, your Honour, is the reply of Mr. Jelavic to the Prime Minister. It is dated 21 February 1997 claiming he is not the legal successor to the archives and requesting that a letter be dispatched to your Honour requesting the suspension of your order of 20 February 1997. I have had this document submitted to translation and I have an official translation of the document attached. The last item I would submit, your Honour, exhibit no. 11, is a letter of 24 February 1997 to Mr. Jelavic from the Prime Minister informing him that the archive of the BH Federation is the legal successor of the HZ HB archive, but that this entity has not started its work and that the documents of the HZ HB archive have not been turned over to the archive of the BH Federation and its also asks that Mr. Jelavic comply with your order of the 20 February I have also submitted this to translation and I have attached a copy of the official translation to this document as well. That concludes my submissions, your Honour. PRESIDING JUDGE: Ms. GLUMAC, I imagine you perhaps have copies of some of these documents but I am not certain that you have copies of all of them, so if you would like we may stand in recess so that copies may be made and provided to you. Is that how you would like to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have most of these documents. I have them in my file here and some that I heard of now, I don’t think they are so important for us that copies should be made and an adjournment made. PRESIDING JUDGE: Mr. Harmon, do you have anything else to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have nothing else to add, your Honour. PRESIDING JUDGE: Judge Vidovic, do you wish to proceed at this time or should we hear from Ms. GLUMAC first?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your honour, I suggest that we first hear Ms. GLUMAC. PRESIDING JUDGE: Ms. GLUMAC

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all I would like to mention some of the circumstances which have led this subpoena that you issued, that it has not been complied with on time. First of all, the war archive of the Croatian community of Herzeg Bosna that these documents that you requested to be submitted to the Tribunal form an integral part of archive. It was controlled or the person in charge of it was the Director who died. And we can provide documents of that. And after his death another person has not been appointed to that position. This archive has also been terminated when all the Herzeg Bosna institutions were terminated. And the hand over of that archive to some other institution of government has not been made. And as far as we know that archive there was information of civilian character as well as information of military character. SO we have information that this archive contained documents and we also have document pertaining to that and you order it to be translated and you can see that this was not an official archive but an archive that contained all the documents pertaining to the war in Herzeg Bosna. In other words, it was an archive that followed the economy, science, cultures, sport and of course the military issues. I would like to submit for the record the decision on establishing the war archive of the Croatian community of Herzeg Bosna and I would like to ask you if it can be translated and present to you right now so that you can see what I am talking about in fact. The Minister of Defence of Herzeg Bosna never played an important part in that archive since the archive was not established as part of the Ministry. The archive was an independent body, it was a government service, and the director of the archive was appointed by the Government of Herzeg Bosna. Is it necessary for me to submit this document to you now? PRESIDING JUDGE: Well yes, you may and we will make it exhibit A or 1 however you want to for Mr. Jelavic. Tell me once more Ms. GLUMAC about this decision. You say that this was a decision establishing the central archive.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: I’m sorry. The decision was made pursuant, actually the Government of the Croatian Community of Herzeg Bosna made the decision to establish this archive. This means that the archive was never part of the Ministry of Defence. The Ministry of Defence was not in charge of the archive. A civilian was at the head of the archive. It was managed by a civilian and part of the archive was of a civilian character. The Director was also appointed by the Government of Herzeg Bosna not by the Ministry, or in other words the Council of Defence. The HVO was only consulted when decision were made on who was to manage the archive. This archive was not the archive of the Ministry of Defence but of the entire community at that time, SO the Defence Ministry of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina cannot be the legal successor of the archive. The archive was supposed to be pursuant to a decision mentioned here in these letters. It was supposed to be succeeded by the archive of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina, established pursuant to a law. The law on Ministerial Bodies and Administrative Body passed after the Dayton agreement in order to facilitate its implementation. Only that archive would be able to distinguish between the civilian and the military documents in the archive, which was formed in Herzeg Bosna. And to process the military information and to pass it on to the Ministry of Defence. This archive has been constituted, established a law on its work has been passed, however the Director has not been appointed yet and it causes additional problems. Since Mr. Jelavic has at no time been involved with this archive and he is not familiar with it because in his work he didn’t have anything to with that archive, he is not able to tell you with any precision what is there. On the other hand, the Ministry of Defence cannot be the legal successor of the archive and the archive of Herzeg Bosna is not the archive of the Ministry of Defence, but of the Community of Herzeg Bosna which existed at the time. In light of all of the above, in light of the fact that Mr. Jelavic never discharged any function related to that archive, I think that it would be good as Mr. Jelavic requested several times so far to request from the competent authorities from the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina and Bosnia Herzegovina the top authorities, since we are dealing with the co-operation with the International Tribunal to ask them to appoint a competent person who will then submit these documents to the Tribunal. Mr. Jelavic thinks that the letter from the Prime Minister quoted by the Prosecutor today is not enough for him to take on without any authorisation documents from the archive and to submit them here. I think this is the problem behind his actions and he is expecting the Ministerial Council or the Presidency to give him authorisation to provide these documents. PRESIDING JUDGE: Why is Mr. Jelavic not here?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Jelavic is prepared to come here before the Tribunal, but he feels that before that these issues should be resolved. The question whether he is authorised to do these things because this whole thing was based on wrong premises. You claim that this is a military archive and that is the archive of then Ministry of Defence and this has led to him , to the Minister of Defence, being declared the legal successor. He wants this issue of competence, who is competent to take over this archive and submit those documents to be settled. Because the archive has never been formally handed over to anyone’s authority. PRESIDING JUDGE: Does Mr. Jelavic

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: This is a very important matter, in particular, because any handle of documents especially military document is such a weighty matter that it reaches the highest level, it jeopardises the co-operation with the tribunal, because some of the documents may jeopardise state security , he feels that he should have authorisation since we are dealing with two entities, he feels that he should have the authority from a higher level, from the Presidency of from the Ministerial Council. PRESIDING JUDGE: He feels that it would be the Presidency of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina, who should direct him?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: That should be a body which would determine whether he is authorised to take this action and to submit documents in this case. PRESIDING JUDGE: Be the Presidency of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: That one or the Ministerial Council. PRESIDING JUDGE: And can you give me the name, the names of the Presidency of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina and the Ministerial Council?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic will provide you with that since she is familiar with that. I am not sure who the members of the Members of the Ministerial Council are PRESIDING JUDGE: If Mr. Jelavic receives instructions from either the Presidency of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina or the Ministerial Council is he prepared to appear?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Of course PRESIDING JUDGE: He will appear? MS. GLUMAC; Yes PRESIDING JUDGE: Now you have indicated that a Director has not been appointed for this war archive. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: The Director of the war archive of the Croatian Community of Herzeg Bosna has died. Mr. Brkic was in that position. After him no successor has been appointed to that post. And after that this institution has ceased to exist because of the overall status of Herzeg Bosna. PRESIDING JUDGE: And when did the former director die?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: I have his death certificate, it happened on the 5th of November 1996. PRESIDING JUDGE: And you have indicated that the war archive no longer continues to exist. So where are those documents to be sent? I gather that another director is not going to be appointed, since the archives don’t exit, or at least, won’t continue. So who has authority for these archives? Archive.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: According to the interpretation and to the legal practice in our parts the legal successor to the archive is definitely the archive of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina. It succeeds this archive and hand over should be done to that institution. The only problem is that the director has not been appointed. The new director of the new archive of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina. And the archive has been established, pursuant to relevant legislation. SO that this archive exists, but it has not been implemented yet, as we say. So what the Prime Minister says in his letter he is asking the hand over from the war archive of Herzeg Bosna to the Ministry of BiH to be effected; although, he claims that the Minister of Defence of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina is not the legal successor but that the legal successor is the newly formed archive formed pursuant to the relevant legislation. That is the archive of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina. PRESIDING JUDGE: And who would this director of the newly formed archive report to? Who would be his superior?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: The Federation of course, the highest bodies of the Federation. It would be an administrative institution. PRESIDING JUDGE: The Presidency of the Federation again?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes PRESIDING JUDGE: Or the Ministerial Council?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: I think the Presidency. PRESIDING JUDGE: OK. You are not familiar with how the archive is organised. Are you ? That is the war archive of Herzeg Bosna. Are you familiar with how it is organised , how the records are organised, where they are maintained, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Only to the extent as it is spelled out in this text of the law, that which says certain ministries are in charge of the work of particular agencies. So that is the text of the law. And what I know in addition to that is that war archive was left behind in Mostar and at no time was any transfer or removal of this archive been attempted. And as I said, as far as the structure of the organisation is concerned, I only know about it as far this text of the law goes. PRESIDING JUDGE: You’ve never been to the war archive, I gather.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: No PRESIDING JUDGE; Does Mr. Jelavic contest the power of the Tribunal, of me to compel his attendance should it be determined that he is the appropriate custodian or representative with respect to these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: No. The only reaction on his part was that this order was a bit too harsh in its language and he also believes that there should be a practice, which has already been established, that if high representatives are coming that they should be invited in a more friendly terms with less drastic written orders, but he does not contest your competence. PRESIDING JUDGE: And if I wrote his a personal letter inviting him to attend?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: I believe he would. With him the problem is not respecting the tribunal, the issue he is contesting is whether it is in his authority to undertake this exercise. In other words, if the issue of his authority is resolved he would undoubtedly come. PRESIDING JUDGE: You know whether Mr. Jelavic is familiar with the way the records are organised in the war archive of what was formerly Herzeg Bosna?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: As far as I know, that was as far as I was told by him, he said that he at no time had any duties which were to put him in contact with the archive. He believes that all the documents were being funnelled into this archive during the war but he says that the documents, the whole archives, the whole working of he had no contact with that. He is not familiar with that. PRESIDING JUDGE: Was there a deputy director, when this director was in charge of the war archives?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: As far as I know there isn’t. The only thing I know is that this director was only an acting director. He was not even appointed to t his position as full time operative, and as far as I know he did not have a deputy either. PRESIDING JUDGE: So who is it then who has control of the war archive of Herzeg Bosna? Who has the key to wherever it is? Who is responsible for making sure that the records remained there?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: I believe that the archive is being kept and taken care of but I don't know who it is. I only know what I have been told and I am not familiar with that aspect, but he information as far as I know, or as far as my information goes, has never been removed or moved from Mostar. PRESIDING JUDGE: Thank you. Judge Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes I would like to explain a couple of issues here. How we arrived at a point to that Mr. Jelavic be identified as the person of authority in this matter. PRESIDING JUDGE: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jelavic was the deputy minister of the Ministry of Defence of Herzeg Bosna and subsequently the Minister of Defence in the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina and he was identified as proposed by the prosecution, as the legal successor of what was formerly the archive of Herzeg Bosna. I need to explain several points so that we know what documents are being requested by the Tribunal and why Mr. Jelavic is identified as a person who has certain information and knowledge about the archives of Herzeg Bosna. The order from the Tribunal explicitly asks, requests the war documents for instance orders for the central Bosnia operation zone and the Ministry of Defence of Herzeg Bosna as well as minutes directed to General Blaskic by Mate Boben or the main staff of Herzeg Bosna and the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian community of Herzeg Bosna and so. In other words these are all documents more or less that are military. And that rightfully belong to the domain of the Ministry of Defence of Herzeg Bosna. I asked about the whereabouts of these documents and I was told that that it was in possession of HVO which has part of the military of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina and so it is absolutely within the domain of the Ministry of Defence which is headed by Mr. Jelavic so that is incontrovertible. As far as the archive of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina is concerned it is true this has not been implemented yet. There has not been transfer of one archive to another and so this archive is still in the possession of the HVO and still under the authority of Mr. Jelavic. SO Mr. Jelavic is indeed the person of authority and he can identify the person who is familiar with this archive and who knows where it is, and what the contents of this archive are. And as far as the authority of the Prime Minister of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina, as you know the Republic of Bosnia Herzegovina consists of two entities, one is the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina and the Prime Minister of the Federation is Mr. Bicakcic, and you have his correspondence with Mr. Jelavic. Mr. Bicakcic is superior to the Minister of Defence and he is the only person who has the authority to issues order to the other ministers. And that is how the Government of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina works. But I am leaving a possibility that this issue be brought up and resolved within the government of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina. PRESIDING JUDGE: What do you mean by that, Judge Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the last point that I made. What I am saying is that Mr. Bicakcic as the Prime Minister of the Federation is authorised to issue orders to his minister including Mr. Jelavic. However, that issue the Tribunal can bring up either with the Prime Minister or any other body of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina and receive a response. Whether the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina is authorise to issue an order to Mr. Jelavic to identify the person who will turn over the documents of the archive or appear here, but I personally believe that it will be a waste of time if we engaged in trying to confirm the fact that seems fairly obvious. But if you want to go ahead and confirm that fact it would be all right with me. PRESIDING JUDGE: Just one question Judge Vidovic. In the letter, I think it is exhibit 10, 8 it’s the letter from Mr. Jelavic to the Prime Minister of the Government of the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina and in paragraph 3 he says that, I think the subpoena is not founded on international law and the statute and rule of the international criminal tribunal. It’s February 19th from Mr. Jelavic

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your question with that respect. PRESIDING JUDGE: He says that only the state can decide who and where will represent it and when it come to co-operation with the ICTY it is represented by the government or more precisely by its office for co-operation with ICTY and not its officials and consequently not by the Defence Minister of the Federation. Are you not, who is the office of co-operation with the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am the authorised representative of Bosnia Herzegovina for contract with the ICTY. And I will explain this in some detail and submit the appropriate documents. I said that I am Minister Counsel with the Embassy of Bosnia Herzegovina, pursuant to a decision of the Presidency of BiH of the 30th July 1994. I was appointed the representative of Bosnia Herzegovina for contacts with the ICTY. And this decision was published in the official gazette on the same day then I received a general authorisation of the Prime Minister of Bosnia Herzegovina and the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina of the 4th June 1994 to attend the hearing when ever the interests of Bosnia Herzegovina are concerned and that was issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia Herzegovina . Both these documents have been submitted to the Registry of the Tribunal but I submit copies of them for the purposes of this hearing to day. PRESIDING JUDGE: They will be accepted. My question really was what he meant by that last paragraph. Because as I understand your position, you believe that he is the proper authority to appear before the Tribunal with respect to these documents that are the subject of the subpoena duces tecum. You have indicated that the Prime Minister has authority to direct him to appear and it seems to me as if he is saying that its your office that co-operates with the tribunal. You have taken a position that either he or someone who is familiar with the records should be here. And that he is the person who has control of those records in his capacity as Minister of Defence. So it seems to me that he won’t listen to your decision, he certain won’t listen to my subpoena, and I don’t know that even if I wrote him he would appear. So, I don’t know. Where are we, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are at a point in this hearing where once again Mr. Jelavic to whom the subpoena has been directed personally has failed to comply with the subpoena duces tecum. The subpoena was issued on 15 January. This is our fourth hearing. He has been directed to appear on three other occasions. He has been asked also to send a representative here, who is familiar with the location and the contents of the archive and to inform this court and the prosecutor’s office what steps have been taken to comply with the subpoena duces tecum. Now what we are met with today is a statement by counsel that essentially there is a dispute as to whether he is the successor. I think the evidence in this case shows that he is the successor. I also refer to exhibit no. 11, which was submitted today from the Prime Minister informing Mr. Jelavic that he still maintains custody of these documents. We have an argument put forth today by counsel that because the custodian of this archive died I think sometime in November that that seems to be the end of the matter. We know for a fact that these archives exist. Mr. Jelavic knows who the custodian of those archives was, he knows where those archives and materials that are responsive to this subpoena are. I haven’t heard a single word today you Honour, through counsel, his representative, specifying what steps have been taken to comply with this subpoena which was issued in January of 1997. Now I believe once again today there an attempt to derail the compliance; with this subpoena and obfiscate the issues. My view is that this subpoena was directed specifically to Mr. Jelavic. He has not shown up. His representative is not prepared to inform this court of what he has been directed to inform it of. And that is where I think we are today. PRESIDING JUDGE: I understand where we are. What I want to know from you is what would you propose that I do. MR. HARMON; I would propose your Honour, that the court find Mr. Jelavic is the successor custodian of central archives and has wilfully failed once again to provide the Tribunal, the office of the Prosecutor with the documents described in the subpoena duces tecum. That he has wilfully failed to designate a representative who could appear before you, who could identify the exact location and the contents of the archives and inform you of what steps have been taken to comply with the subpoena duces tecum. That by failing to comply with the subpoena duces tecum Mr. Jelavic has obstructed the office of the prosecutor’s investigation and preparation or the case of the Prosecutor v. Blaskic, that Mr. Jelavic be found in contempt of this court and that your Honour order him personally to appear before you to explain why he should not be punished for that contempt. Should be fail to appear, your honour, we will be requesting this court to issue a warrant for his arrest. PRESIDING JUDGE: The Prime Minister says in his letter of 24 February to Mr. Jelavic in his capacity as Defence Minister, he says in the last paragraph, he talks about the archives of Herzeg Bosna and he then says considering the above and bearing in mind that the documents pertain to defence matters and the fact that as the Federal Defence Minister you are in a position to have the most knowledge of the matter, it is my opinion that grounds for seeking a suspension of your obligations pursuant to the order of the ICTY judge don’t exist and I ask that you comply with the obligations arising from the order. That the exhibit you were referring to. Thank you Mr. Harmon. Ms. GLUMAC do you have a response to the prosecutor’s proposals as to how I should proceed given Mr. Jelavic’s failure to appear and failure to have someone who is familiar with the records appear to day.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that the fact that he does not believe he is the person of authority to handle the archive and does not have the authorisation of the highest authorities of the Federation is what is really the point here rather than his intentional obfuscation or failure comply with the order of the Tribunal. And what you have quoted now even Mr. Bicakcic accepted the fact that the archive of BH Federation is not the legal successor of the HBHV in other words the Prime Minister himself as is stated in the second paragraph of the letter agrees with Mr. Jelavic that he is not the legal successor of the archive. He is just giving him and additional obligation, a duty to take over this obligation and become involve in the transfer of the archive, so I think that really it is a question of making clear who is authorised, rather than an intention to not comply with the orders of this tribunal. So, I propose that the proposal of late prosecutor not be accepted. PRESIDING JUDGE: Doesn’t the Prime Minister say that even though, he says I agree with your conclusion that the archive of the BH Federation is the legal successor to the HB archive, however, you know that such an institution administrative organisation does not exist at the level of the BH Federation, and then he says since a director of the archive of the BH Federation has never been appointed and pursuant to the above cited legal provisions the archive of the Federation has not started its work. Subsequently the documents and items have never been properly turned over to the archive of the BH Federation by the HZHB archive. And then he says considering the above and bearing in mind that the documents pertain to defence matters and the fact that as the Federal Defence Minister you are in a position to have the most knowledge of the matter, it is my opinion the grounds for seeking a suspension of your obligations do not exist and I ask you to comply. SO what he is saying, he’s telling him as his superior that he does have responsibility for those documents because they are defence documents. And that there is no archive I gather . There is no director of the archive of the BH Federation but he is saying that even though there is no director because items requested relate to defence matters he has the authority. I gather Mr. Jelavic disagrees. He says he doesn’t have the authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: But your Honour, also it states here that it is only now that Mr. Jelavic should take over and become involve in the transfer of the archive to the BH Federation archive. In other words, he is saying that Mr. Jelavic up until now had no legal authority over these documents but now he should take over the documents and the archive of the Herzeg Bosna, because my understanding is that this archive wasn’t attached to the Ministry of Defence of Herzeg Bosna. It was a general sort of community archive. But now he is ordering him to take over these documents. in other words he is not taking over these archives because there is not director there but he is telling him to take over these documents which does not mean a non compliance. It points to the fact that the whole issue of the legal successor has not been resolved up until then, but the archive does exist, it has been established by law, but no director or no head of the archive has ever been appointed. And now for the first time we are talking about an authorisation to take custody of these documents of the former archive of Herzeg Bosna.~ PRESIDING JUDGE: Mr. Jelavic then accepts the authority of the Prime Minister Bicakcic to direct him to take over control of documents of the HZHB archive, the legal successor for which was the archive of the Bosnia Herzegovina Federation, but no director has been appointed. But is he authorising Mr. Jelavic to take control of those documents that pertain to defence matters that are in the archive? Is that how you read this letter? That’s what I understand you to have said.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, that’s what he states here. He authorises him at this moment to take over those documents at this time. I think that nowhere it has been mentioned as Madam Vidovic said that there exists as a separate entity the war archives of HZHB as an exclusively military archive. PRESIDING JUDGE: Does Mr. Jelavic accept that the Prime Minister, Bicakcic has that authority to direct that he take over those documents that pertain to defence matters?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: The only thing that I know is what I have already told you that he asks the competent authorities in the Federation of Bosnia Herzegovina to make a decision as to the authority. If this letter was confirmed by them I don’t think that we would have any problems. PRESIDING JUDGE: And who is them, that would have to confirm the decision of the Prime Minister Bicakcic? Can you give me their names and the positions that they hold?

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: I think the Presidency or the Ministerial Council. My learned colleague will be able to supply you with the names. I don’t know who the members are of the Ministerial Council. I think there are three members. I don't know either. We can supply the names. PRESIDING JUDGE: Judge Vidovic has told us that the Prime Minister has this authority. She has told us that it is not necessary to go any further. I gather you disagree. But you don’t know the names of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic also said that my claims can be confirmed, verified PRESIDING JUDGE: Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I stated very clearly that the Prime minister of any government is authorised to issue orders to his ministers, members of his cabinet. So the Prime Minister, Bicakcic, is in any case authorised to issue an order to any of his minister including Mr. Jelavic of course. PRESIDING JUDGE: How do you propose we handle this difference of opinion about the authority of the Prime Minister? Or do you consider it relevant to the orders that have been issued by me regarding Mr. Jelavic? MR. HARMON; Your Honour, if I were essentially to wait until a political dispute is resolved I could be here until well after the trial starts. This subpoena very clearly directed Mr. Jelavic on certain terms very clearly to be here, to designate a representative who could inform the court of the location of the archives, to inform the court of the contents of the archives and to inform the court of what steps since 15 January 1997 have been taken to comply with this subpoena duces tecum. I think the issues that have been raised by counsel are issues that are not relevant to your order directing Mr. Jelavic to be here personally or designate a knowledgeable representative. I would inform the court in one of the previous hearings I submitted an exhibit, I don’t have the number unfortunately, your Honour, but it is a letter from the Prime Minister dated 21 February 1997, to Mr. Jelavic asking him to obey the order of this court. Mr. Jelavic has been asked to obey the order of this court by your Honour, he’s been asked to obey the order of the court by the Prime Minister. These archives, just because the custodian died, these archives didn’t disappear. From what I am hearing from counsel, they remain in the same place and we have every right to know what steps have been taken to comply with this subpoena duces tecum. From what I gather, since I haven’t received a single document, no attempts have been made to comply with the subpoena duces tecum. I think, your Honour’s question was very direct and to the point, who has the key to the archives. Is Mr. Jelavic saying that he doesn’t have actual control over those archives? We have been informed by the representative of the Federation and the Bosnian government that he is the legal successor. We have been informed in exhibit 11 that I submitted today that the Prime Minister has said those documents have not been transferred to this new entity, this new archive, and clearly Mr. Jelavic has, we believe, actual control over these archives. Bear in mind, your Honour, that the previous hearing in response to this subpoena duces tecum, we received, it could have been in response to the subpoena duces tecum or it could have been in response to a request for co-operation we made on 2 May 1996. We received 11 documents. These documents must have come from some place. My view is, your Honour, that there is non-compliance to this day with the subpoena duces tecum. Mr. Jelavic has been given four opportunities to comply with this subpoena duces tecum, and I would again reiterate my request. PRESIDING JUDGE: The concern that I have, Ms. GLUMAC, is that in his letter Mr. Jelavic letter of 19 Feb. he says that only a state can decide who and where will represent it and when it comes to co-operation with International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia it is represented by the government or more precisely by its office for co-operation with ICTY. And not its officials and consequently not by the Defence Minister. I read that to say saying that the office for co-operation with the ICTY is responsible for co-operating with ICTY and what Madam Vidovic has told us is that Mr. Jelavic should comply with this subpoena. He’s been told to comply by the Prime Minister and he should comply. And so if I am to accept his position that he states in his letter of 19 February, he’s certainly aware of Madam Vidovic’s position as the Minister counsel and as the person in charge of the office for co-operation with ICTY. She herself, I believe, has communicated with him. Am I correct about that? Yes. And so he knows what her position is. So if he is now recognising that office then that office has also told him to comply.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Your Honour, on the other hand we have the thing that I mentioned before these are the documents that are in the majority at least partly fall into the category of state secrets. Some of the documents have to do with the state security, so he feels that with these kind of documents he would need additional authorisation, additional permission. PRESIDING JUDGE: We have a rule that governs that situation and it allows for a person who takes that position regarding documents that may constitute state secrets or may affect their security for those documents to be examined in camera by the judge to make that determination. So then pursuant to that rule I would be more than willing to examine the documents if that has been his concern. But what I am saying is that at one point he says it’s the office of co-operation with ICTY whose responsible and that person, Madam Vidovic, has said and has asked him to come. So he won’t listen then to the office of co-operation with ICTY, he won’t listen to the Prime Minister, he won’t listen to my orders. And when I say listen, what I mean is comply. So I don’t know how else to get him here. You said, I am sure you were saying it in jest, that if I wrote him, if I spoke to him in less direct term he would be here. I would be happy to attach a letter to this order that will enter that will encourage him to come.

utterances.speaker: MS. GLUMAC
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me just add. I don’t think that this has been interpreted in the correct manner, despite of the letter indicating that only the office for co-operation with ICTY are authorised. to work with the Tribunal. He was trying to say that all the activity of the state towards the Tribunal goes through the office. He did not mean any disrespect. He just wanted to say that the office is authorised for any co-operation and not he as an individual. That is what he meant. He did not mean any disrespect for any decisions of judge Vidovic or he didn’t mean any disrespect of you. PRESIDING JUDGE: Now, Mr. Jelavic is not appeared. It certainly would have been more appropriate for him to appear to provide us, to provide me with answers regarding his duties, regarding he knowledge of the archive. You certainly are not a representative. And all he has said in letters that he is not the representative. We have many letters from the Prime Minster directing him to be here. And then once he comes of course, if he did come then I could enquire of him regarding his responsibilities. But first he must come here as directed, and even if the Prime Minister is wrong about whether he has control, or whether the has the documents. The point is that the Prime Minister has directed that he be here and the Prime Minister, it seems to me, is the person who is responsible for exercising the state’s obligation under article 29 of our statute and many other section of the statute and our rules to co-operate operate with the tribunal, and he has co-operated and he has directed him to be here.. So it appears to me that he is not complying with that directive nor with the subpoena duces tecum, which is the underlying request. If nothing else is to be added by you, then Mr. Harmon or Ms. GLUMAC, or Madam Vidovic I will take this matter under advisement and issue an order either today regarding this matter or on Monday. But I don’t think Mr. Jelavic will be here no matter how we ask him to be here. And that’s unfortunate because we need to resolve the issue of the subpoena, the documents requested in the subpoena. So we will adjourn.
